Texas: what's on the November 3, 2026 ballot

Every candidate below is listed alphabetically, with party shown as text only. Open a name for their stated positions, background and recent news, each with sources.

Open Texas on the map

Key dates

  • Voter registration deadline: October 5, 2026. Last day to register or update your registration.
  • Early voting: October 19, 2026 to October 30, 2026. Vote at any early voting site in your county. Hours vary by county.
  • Last day to apply for a mail ballot: October 23, 2026. The application must be received by your county's early voting clerk.
  • General Election Day: November 3, 2026. Polls open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Mail ballots must arrive by 7 p.m. (Nov. 4 at 5 p.m. if postmarked by Election Day).

Official election information: VoteTexas.gov

Certified write-in candidates and the Texas House, Texas Senate, State Board of Education and district court races aren't loaded yet.

State

Governor

Head of the state executive branch. Four-year term.

  • Greg Abbott Republican · Incumbent
    Governor since 2015, seeking a fourth term. Polls in September and early October showed a close race; a YouGov poll from Sept. 28 to Oct. 5 had Hinojosa at 48% and Abbott at 47%,…
  • Pat Dixon Libertarian · Challenger
    Former chair of the Libertarian Party of Texas. Polled between 1% and 6% when included. No campaign positions were found in our sources.
  • Gina Hinojosa Democratic · Challenger
    Represents Austin's House District 49 since 2017. Won the March 3 Democratic primary with about 58.5% of the vote.

Lieutenant Governor

Presides over the Texas Senate and controls much of its agenda. Independent Mike Collier sought a spot but a federal court declined to add him to the ballot.

  • Anthony Cristo Libertarian · Challenger
    Libertarian nominee for Congress in Texas's 15th District in 2018 and 34th District in 2020. No campaign positions were found in our sources.
  • Vikki Goodwin Democratic · Challenger
    Austin state representative who flipped a Republican-held House seat in 2018. Won the May 26 runoff with 67.8%. Reported about $643,000 cash on hand in the latest filings.
  • Kevin McCormick Green · Challenger
    Former teacher. No campaign positions were found in our sources.
  • Dan Patrick Republican · Incumbent
    Lieutenant governor since 2015. Endorsed by President Trump and Gov. Abbott. Reported about $24 million cash on hand in the latest filings.

Attorney General

The state's chief lawyer. Open seat because Ken Paxton is running for U.S. Senate.

  • Nathan Johnson Democratic · Open seat
    Texas Senate since 2019 representing part of Dallas County. Won the May 26 runoff with 60.5%.
  • Mayes Middleton Republican · Open seat
    Texas Senate since 2023 after four years in the Texas House. Won the May 26 runoff over U.S. Rep. Chip Roy with 55.2%. University of Texas School of Law graduate.
  • Tom Oxford Libertarian · Open seat
    Has practiced law since 1982. The Texas Tribune found no public information on his policy stances.
